input.quote: Except as stated in Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6, this Agreement may not be assigned by the Depositor or the Servicer without the consent of the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee, the Certificateholders and the Noteholders of at least 66-2/3% of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class.
input.rationale: Section 10.2(a) is the operative assignment clause. Our side is protected on the outbound leg: Section 5.3 (p0249) lets the Depositor pass this Agreement to a merger/consolidation successor, a person succeeding to its business, or an Affiliate, and Section 10.2(a) expressly excepts Section 5.3 from the consent requirement. Section 7.1 (p0314) also bars the Servicer from resigning except on legal inability, so a change of control on our side gives Cellco no exit. The clause fails on the inbound leg. Section 10.2(a) requires consents from the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders and Noteholders, but not from the Issuer or the Depositor, so we hold no consent right over a Servicer assignment; the consent standard is unqualified rather than "not unreasonably withheld"; there is no bar on assignment to a competitor; and the Section 7.6 carve-out (p0348) lets Cellco assign to any Cellco Affiliate with no consent or notice at all, which also defeats the fallback requirement that every non-successor assignment need consent. The redline removes the Section 7.6 exception for the Servicer only, adds the Issuer's reasonable consent, and adds a competitor bar, leaving Section 5.3 and the Section 7.4 successor-servicer mechanics intact. Ancillary point noted but not flagged: Section 6.4 (p0300) allows consent-free delegation while Cellco remains Servicer, but delegation does not relieve Cellco of responsibility.

proposal.summary: Require the Issuer's reasonable consent to any Servicer assignment (including to a Cellco Affiliate) and bar assignment to a competitor, leaving the Depositor's Section 5.3 affiliate/successor rights untouched.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that the Servicer may not assign without our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor, while we keep our Section 5.3 affiliate and successor rights. We therefore removed the Section 7.6 carve-out that lets Cellco assign to its own Affiliate consent-free and added the Issuer's reasonable consent plus a competitor bar.

ops.newText: Except as stated in Sections 5.3 and 7.4, this Agreement may not be assigned by the Depositor or the Servicer without the consent of the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee, the Certificateholders and the Noteholders of at least 66-2/3% of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class, and, for the Servicer, the Issuer, whose consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

ops.text: The Servicer may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of the Issuer or the Depositor.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
mappings.quote: (d) that is an Affiliate of the Depositor to whom the Depositor has assigned this Agreement, will be the successor to the Depositor under this Agreement.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
mappings.quote: Any Person (a) into which the Depositor is merged or consolidated, (b) resulting from a merger or consolidation to which the Depositor is a party, (c) succeeding to the Depositor's business

mappings.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
mappings.quote: The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
